reasoning.title: Exhaustive paginated review audit
reasoning.description: Use when asked to identify every reviewer whose text discusses a concept or close paraphrase; do not use for tasks requesting only an aggregate review count or a single known review.
reasoning.content: On the product page, open the visible “Reviews” tab or review-count link, then read every review card and follow every “Page”/“Next” link; “Add Your Review” is a submission form, and site search is not a review-content filter. Match the full review meaning rather than only an exact phrase, record every qualifying “Review by” value, and verify each name in a clean rendering or another page/detail view when the list duplicates or abbreviates text; deduplicate rows without preserving display artifacts, and compare the final list against all marked matches before answering.

reasoning.title: Exhaustive paginated review verification
reasoning.description: Use for tasks asking which reviewers mention a concept on a product page; do not use product details or site search as substitutes for the customer-review list.
reasoning.content: Open the visible “Reviews” tab, read every review title and body, and follow all “Page”/“Next” links, including related wording rather than only exact phrases; record every qualifying row only when its text is visible. Pair each match with its adjacent “Review by” value, and when pagination repeats a row or concatenates a name, verify it on another page or detail view and copy the clean full displayed name exactly, checking the final list for omissions, duplicates, and near-identical variants.

reasoning.title: Exhaust paginated reviews and verify reviewer names
reasoning.description: Apply when identifying every reviewer whose review mentions a requested concept; do not use the catalog Search or Advanced Search controls, which find products rather than filter review text.
reasoning.content: Open the product’s “Reviews” tab, read every review row in full, and follow each “Page” or “Next” link until no review pages remain; record every qualifying row, including indirect or near-variant wording, only when the relevant text is visibly present. Before answering, reconcile repeated rows across pages and copy the cleanest fully displayed “Review by” value from another page or detail view rather than preserving a duplicated, truncated, or otherwise malformed rendering.

reasoning.title: Exhaustive paginated review scan
reasoning.description: Apply when a task asks which reviewers mention a phrase, attribute, or closely related wording; do not use this process for product details unrelated to customer reviews.
reasoning.content: Open the product page’s “Reviews” tab or review-count link, not “Add Your Review,” then inspect every review body and follow all “Page” or “Next” links, accounting for repeated rows across pages. Record every row containing the requested wording or a plausible textual variant—even if its referent seems unexpected—and verify each inclusion directly against visible text. Copy the reviewer name exactly from the clearest display; if a listing concatenates or abbreviates it, confirm it on another page or detail view rather than guessing or treating near-identical forms as different people.

reasoning.title: Exhaustive review scan and identity normalization
reasoning.description: Use when a shopping task asks which reviewers mention a phrase, attribute, or condition; do not use product search, “Add Your Review,” or summary ratings as substitutes for reading existing review text.
reasoning.content: On the product page, open the visible “Reviews” tab, read every review body, and follow all “Page”/“Next” pagination controls; treat the review-count link only as a shortcut, not as proof that all reviews are displayed. Include every visibly matching row, including awkward, typo-like, or weakly contextual wording containing the requested concept, rather than narrowing by inferred intent. Copy the complete “Review by” value, open a fuller view if abbreviated, reconcile repeated reviews across pages, normalize obvious duplicated rendering of the same name, and verify near-identical variants against another visible rendering instead of guessing.

reasoning.title: Review all paginated feedback with broad semantic matching
reasoning.description: Use when a shopping task asks which reviewers mention a concept; do not restrict matches to exact wording or only the most explicit statements, and do not stop after the first review page.
reasoning.content: Open the product page’s “Reviews” tab, read every review title and body, and follow all “Page” or “Next” links, accounting for reviews repeated across page boundaries. Include every visible row whose wording references the requested concept directly or indirectly, then copy the reviewer name from “Review by”; if that name is duplicated or malformed in one view, verify it on another page or detail view rather than guessing.

reasoning.title: Audit every review match before compiling names
reasoning.description: Use when identifying reviewers whose feedback mentions a requested feature or issue; do not use site search or “Add Your Review” as review-content filters.
reasoning.content: Open the product’s visible “Reviews” tab or review-count link, read every review card in full, and follow all numbered “Page” or “Next” controls, including indirect, awkward, or typo-like wording that visibly expresses the requested concept. Record each match with its adjacent “Review by” value immediately, then reconcile the final list against every recorded match; deduplicate repeated rows, but verify concatenated, abbreviated, or near-identical names in a cleaner pagination rendering or detail view and copy the complete displayed name rather than guessing.
